statement: Partition-key ordering has one complete owner: compareRoutingKeys supplies deterministic SQLite-BINARY-compatible UTF-8 TEXT/string order, including non-BMP keys, while preserving the already-landed numeric-vs-text-encoded-number order and exact typed mixed-space refusal; KeyRange, PartitionResolver, QueryGroup and both split/merge sort and adjacency consume that owner for partition keys, with no merge-adjacency raw relational partition-key comparator remaining.

constraints.statement: Supersedes partition-key-ordering-owner-completion because independent pre-seal review found that its checker lacked a non-BMP UTF-8/BINARY discriminator and accepted any thrown error as mixed-key refusal. The original sealed predicate stays immutable.

Preserve the solved numeric-key-routing contract: a number against a text-encoded numeric partition boundary compares numerically, number/number remains numeric, and an unrelated mixed key space is refused with the exact typed split-key mismatch outcome.

The 0.3 persisted TEXT-key baseline is deterministic SQLite BINARY-compatible UTF-8 byte order, not host-locale or JavaScript UTF-16 relational order. Behavioral proof includes a BMP/non-BMP pair whose order differs under UTF-16 code units.

Merge sorting, merge adjacency, KeyRange, PartitionResolver and QueryGroup consume the same partition-key ordering owner. A table-id sort may use a separate stable identifier comparator but must not become or reuse a second partition-key semantic owner.

Do not absorb numeric precision, persisted type metadata, encoding migration or old-boundary revalidation into this Quest. Record those representation findings for A2 partition-key-boundary-representation.

This Quest changes no Raft runtime, consensus transport, replica lifecycle, membership or formation behavior. It may be developed while raft-rs-full-cutover finishes, but it is not merged to shared main ahead of that cutover's exact-head closeout.

Use deterministic behavioral witnesses against real SQLite BINARY ordering and merge-adjacency owner consumption. Reverting each load-bearing semantic change must make the corresponding witness red; the structural doneWhen checker alone is not sufficient proof.

Any src/ change requires an independent verification newer than the last attempt. The verifier attacks duplicate comparison owners, coercion/locale dependence, non-BMP ordering, hostile mixed input, and controlled-negative fidelity with concrete evidence paths.

Capture relevant file-scoped complexity, literal/runtime-grammar and file-size status before production edits and finish with no increased guardrail debt; generated test metadata is refreshed through its producer, never edited by hand.
